chunks: And the Shaykh, may Allah the Exalted support him, informed me from Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, from Aḥmad ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb and al-Ḥasan ibn Mūsā al-Khashshāb together, from Yazīd ibn Isḥāq Shaʿīr, from Hārūn ibn Ḥamzah al-Ghanawī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a mouse, a scorpion, and the like that fall into water and then come out alive: may that water be drunk from and wudu (ablution) be performed with it? He said: "Three times of it are poured out, and its small amount and large amount are of one status. Then one may drink from it and perform wudu (ablution) with it, except for the gecko, for one does not benefit from what it falls into."

This is when the mouse has not decomposed. But if it has decomposed, then seven buckets are drawn from the water, as indicated by the two previous reports, one of which al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Qāsim, from ʿAlī, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mouse falling into a well, and he said: "Seven buckets."

And also the report that al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said: I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a mouse falling into the well, or a bird. He said: "If you reach it before it stinks, draw seven buckets from it."

We only interpreted these two reports to mean the case when the mouse has decomposed, so that the reports do not contradict one another and so that we would not reject what we have narrated that includes three buckets. And another hadith has also come indicating what we have held.

key_terms.تَفَسَّخَتْ: decomposed or disintegrated, affecting the legal ruling
key_terms.سَبْعُ دِلَاءٍ: seven buckets to be drawn in the specified case
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: wudu (ablution) is performed using the water
key_terms.يُنْزَحُ: water is drawn out from the well
key_terms.ٱلْعَقْرَبِ: the scorpion mentioned among creatures falling into water
key_terms.ٱلْفَأْرَةِ: the mouse discussed in the ruling of water contamination
key_terms.ٱلْوَزَغِ: the gecko, excluded from permitted benefit in this report

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on water or well-water when a mouse or similar creature falls into it in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on water into which a mouse, scorpion, or similar creature falls and emerges alive. It indicates that the water may still be used after pouring out three portions, except in the case of the gecko; and it further distinguishes the case where a mouse has decomposed, in which case seven buckets are to be drawn. The passage also preserves a juristic reconciliation between apparently differing reports.
